title: Bangladesh to form wage board after garment protests shut factories
full_text:
DHAKA, Nov 1 (Reuters) - Bangladesh will set up a wage board on Sunday to review garment workers’ pay after protests shut dozens of factories and triggered clashes with police, putting fresh strain on the country’s key export industry.
Workers in the South Asian nation are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($245), more than double the current 12,500 taka, saying rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare have sharply eroded their purchasing power.
The dispute has raised concerns about disruption to an industry that employs about 4 million workers, generates more than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings and supplies clothing to many leading Western brands.
Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the government would formally constitute the wage board after discussions with labour leaders and industry representatives aimed at defusing the unrest.
Saturday’s protests prompted about 30 garment factories in Ashulia, a key manufacturing hub on the outskirts of Dhaka, to declare holidays, said Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of the Ashulia Industrial Police.
Hundreds of workers blocked a major intersection in the capital, while demonstrations in other industrial zones disrupted traffic and factory operations. Clashes between workers and police in Ashulia injured several people, including police officers, police said. Officers used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters.
Chowdhury urged workers to return to work, saying the government’s decision to review the wage structure addressed their key demand.
He warned that prolonged factory closures and production disruptions could delay export shipments and payments from international buyers, creating further difficulties for manufacturers and workers.
Bangladesh’s ready-made garment industry, the world’s largest after China, contributes about 10% of gross domestic product and is the backbone of the economy.
Manufacturers, however, said the sector is facing mounting challenges, including rising production costs, periodic gas and electricity shortages, and uncertainty in energy markets linked to tensions in the Middle East.

title: AI investors rush to hedge against potential tech market downturn - WSJ
full_text:
Investing.com -- Investors and technology executives are increasingly seeking protection against a potential artificial intelligence market downturn as concerns mount over the sustainability of trillions of dollars in AI-related investments, The Wall Street Journal reported Saturday.
Demand for hedging instruments, including put options and credit-default swaps, has accelerated following sharp declines in technology stocks and growing concerns about the financial risks associated with AI infrastructure spending.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% Friday, recording its worst monthly performance since March 2025, as investors reassessed valuations across the technology sector.
CoreWeave, a major AI infrastructure provider, has attracted particularly strong demand for downside protection.
Trading volumes for put options tied to the company reached record levels in October, according to Cboe Global Markets data.
Popular contracts include options expiring in 2028 that would benefit from CoreWeave shares falling to $35, compared with approximately $55 recently.
Concerns have also spread to corporate debt markets.
The cost of insuring against defaults by Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle recently climbed to its highest level since 2021, according to bond data provider Solve.
Oracle experienced particularly sharp deterioration, with its credit-default swap spreads widening by more than one percentage point.
Trading firms are developing new financial products to address risks associated with AI computing infrastructure.
Jump Trading has launched a computing-power trading desk offering derivatives designed to protect data center operators against falling chip rental prices.
Rental rates for Nvidia B300 chips have increased approximately 56% this year to $7.56 per hour, according to Silicon Data.
The contracts could protect operators against a future decline in rental rates as computing capacity expands.
Susquehanna International Group is also receiving interest from data centers and private AI infrastructure providers seeking protection against semiconductor-related risks.
Some proposed contracts would track computing-power indexes, potentially helping operators secure financing by limiting exposure to falling rental revenues.
Despite growing hedging activity, demand for protection remains relatively small compared with the broader AI investment boom.

title: Trump calls $50 million contract for ex-lawyer Habba Mildon ’not acceptable’
full_text:
By Gram Slattery and Jasper Ward
PALM BEACH, Oct 31 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Saturday it was "unacceptable" for one of his former lawyers, Alina Habba Mildon, to secure a $50 million contract for herself while working at the US Department of Justice.
"I thought it was totally obnoxious and outrageous, and it’s not acceptable," Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida. "Not acceptable at all."
The New York Times reported last week that the family of Julio Herrera Velutini, a Venezuelan banker facing US felony bribery charges before striking a plea deal in August 2025, guaranteed Habba Mildon more than $50 million over four years. The deal, according to the newspaper, would pay $10 million a year plus bonuses.
Trump said he told Habba Mildon he did not want her to be paid and called the episode "terrible."
Habba Mildon was serving as the acting US attorney in New Jersey when she signed the contract with Herrera’s family company, Concord Partners, days after it was registered in late October 2025, the New York Times reported.
By the time she started her employment with the Herrera family, a court had disqualified her from serving as US attorney. She resigned on December 8 and was appointed a senior adviser to the attorney general the same day, and was still in that role when, according to the New York Times, she started at Concord on January 1.
Trump pardoned Herrera on January 15, 2026, according to the Justice Department’s website.
Habba Mildon last week said she was never paid for a pardon, never met with anyone at the White House or Justice Department about a pardon, and never did any work for a pardon for anyone.
The Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Apple overtakes Nvidia to become world’s most valuable company amid tech selloff
full_text:
Investing.com -- Apple Inc (NASDAQ:AAPL) reclaimed its position as the world’s most valuable publicly traded company on Friday, edging past NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) as mounting skepticism surrounding aggressive artificial intelligence spending prompted a rotation into more capital-disciplined balance sheets. Even with a 1.2% dip on the day, the iPhone maker closed with a market capitalization of $5.03 trillion, while a 4.2% slide in Nvidia lowered the chipmaker’s valuation to $4.93 trillion.
The milestone marks the first time Apple has surpassed Nvidia since a brief stint in late July. Broad tech weakness intensified after quarterly updates from Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) and Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) deepened anxiety over the immediate returns on unprecedented investments in AI infrastructure, following earlier disappointments from Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Meta Platforms Inc (NASDAQ:META).
Wall Street’s retreat from tech leaders has been steep, reflected by monthly slides of 18.6% in Alphabet and 15.2% in Meta, alongside a single-session collapse of nearly 30% for Intel. Nvidia itself has shed 10% over the past month, signaling that the primary beneficiaries of the semiconductor buildout not immune to broader scrutiny over corporate end-demand.
Against that backdrop, Apple’s measured stance on infrastructure investment has transformed the stock into a preferred haven within the Magnificent Seven cohort. Shares are up 27% year-to-date, more than double Nvidia’s second-place advance, bolstered by a 3% gain over the past month that diverged sharply from peers.
The divergence highlights mounting institutional focus on balance sheet health, particularly as soaring capital commitments begin to erode fundamental cash generation among hyper-scalers. Alphabet disclosed negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion for the third quarter, while Amazon reported a trailing twelve-month negative free cash flow deficit of $42.4 billion as infrastructure deployment accelerated.
With borrowing costs elevated, peers have increasingly turned to debt markets to bridge those cash deficits rather than relying strictly on organic operational funding. Apple, by contrast, is expected to generate expanding free cash flow, offering investors immediate liquidity resilience while the broader sector navigates a protracted wait for enterprise AI monetization.

title: Iran offers 48-hour Hormuz reopening plan as Trump signals progress in talks
full_text:
Investing.com -- Iran has proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington meets its conditions, offering a breakthrough in talks to end the war as both sides warn that renewed fighting could spread regionally.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Qatari mediators had helped shorten Tehran’s seven-day reopening proposal. Under the revised sequence, the U.S. would take steps on the first day, and shipping would resume on the second.
President Donald Trump said negotiations were “going fine” and Iran wanted a deal, although he added that Washington was not in a hurry. He also renewed threats against Iranian nuclear facilities, including the site known as Pickaxe Mountain.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not decided whether to launch fresh strikes and that a diplomatic settlement remained possible. An Iranian delegation was in Doha for consultations with mediators, with no direct U.S.-Iran talks planned.
Tehran’s demands include sanctions relief, the release of frozen funds, restored oil waivers, and recognition of a shipping route designated with Oman. Iran also wants a reduced U.S. military presence and an end to attacks on Lebanon.
Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said a letter from Vice President JD Vance signaled a more conciliatory U.S. tone, but insisted Tehran would not reopen Hormuz before its conditions were met.
The diplomatic opening came alongside escalating military warnings. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered commanders to prepare an immediate response to any attack without geographical restrictions, and Iranian officials threatened strikes against a wider range of targets.
Shipping risks remain acute. Iran’s navy said a tanker caught fire after striking mines east of Hormuz, without identifying the vessel or reporting the crew’s condition. U.S. Central Command said its blockade of Iranian ports had redirected 144 commercial ships.
Disruption to the waterway continues to threaten global energy supplies. Germany’s gas storage industry warned that reserves stood at 61.35% ahead of winter, below the country’s 80% target, partly reflecting war-driven energy costs.
The coming days could test whether the proposed shipping arrangement can advance before Washington and Tehran resolve their disputes.

title: Binance to resume crypto withdrawals in phases after record $6 billion hack
full_text:
Investing.com -- Binance said it would begin restoring customer withdrawals in stages on Sunday after a record cryptocurrency theft exceeding $6 billion forced the world’s largest digital asset exchange to suspend transactions and raised concerns about security across the industry.
The exchange said the first phase would run from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m. Singapore time on November 1, with additional cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks restored after security and stability checks.
Binance said it would prioritize assets based on customer withdrawal demand over the previous week, allowing services to resume gradually rather than reopening all transactions simultaneously.
The announcement follows a breach disclosed Thursday that prompted Binance to halt withdrawals early Friday in Asia.
The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group, which was previously linked to the $1.5 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit in 2025.
Binance said it had replaced approximately 90% of the stolen cryptocurrencies and reiterated that customers would not bear the financial losses.
The stolen assets included Bitcoin, Ether and dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC.
Co-CEO Richard Teng said the exchange could cover the losses through cryptocurrency holdings accumulated from its operating revenue.
Fellow co-CEO Yi He indicated that Binance’s annual revenue would be sufficient to absorb the financial impact.
Bitcoin traded near $77,700 on Sunday, approximately 5% below its Thursday high before the attack, as major cryptocurrencies showed relatively limited price movements.
The exchange holds approximately $135 billion in assets, significantly exceeding the roughly $29 billion held by rival OKX, according to DefiLlama.
Binance also maintains its Secure Asset Fund for Users, established in 2018 to protect customers during exceptional incidents. The emergency reserve has typically been maintained near $1 billion.
Investigators are examining a potentially compromised software engineer’s laptop and other possible entry points, although Binance said it had found no evidence that private wallet keys were exposed.
The incident has intensified scrutiny of cryptocurrency security amid concerns that hackers are increasingly using artificial intelligence for reconnaissance and social engineering.

title: Bitcoin faces further downside risks as fear surges, Binance hack rattles markets
full_text:
Investing.com -- Bitcoin entered November under pressure after a sharp deterioration in investor sentiment, heavy exchange-traded fund outflows, and a record $6.3 billion Binance hack raised concerns that the cryptocurrency’s recent selloff may not be over.
Bitcoin fell approximately 7.3% in October, closing the month near $77,558 after opening at around $83,554. The cryptocurrency was trading at $77,820.0 as of 01:17 ET (05:17 GMT) on November 1, up 0.76% on the day, after touching a monthly low of $76,314 during the October selloff.
The Crypto Fear and Greed Index plunged from 70 on October 4 to 36 by October 30, shifting from greed to fear in less than four weeks.
Historical comparisons suggest caution. During three previous declines exceeding 30 index points within a month, Bitcoin traded lower 30 days later, although the sample offers no reliable prediction of future prices.
Institutional selling added pressure. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $643.3 million in net outflows on October 30, their largest daily withdrawal of the month, reversing four consecutive sessions of inflows.
Cumulative ETF inflows fell to approximately $57 billion, compared with an October peak of $57.8 billion.
Derivatives markets also signaled heightened risk. Bitcoin futures open interest reached a five-week high of 686,000 BTC, with long positions accounting for 79% of liquidations.
Bitfinex analysts identified $75,000 as a key support level, with a sustained recovery requiring Bitcoin to reclaim $80,000.
Meanwhile, the FBI attributed Binance’s unprecedented cryptocurrency theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking group.
Investigators said the attackers were converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum before potentially laundering proceeds through decentralized finance platforms and cryptocurrency swap services.
The FBI urged crypto businesses to block transactions involving identified addresses, as blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis warned that thousands of wallets were already involved.
Binance said it had replenished approximately 90% of the stolen assets and pledged to absorb customer losses.
Strategy Executive Chairman Michael Saylor backed the exchange’s reimbursement commitment, predicting stronger industry security following the breach.
The turbulence coincided with Bitcoin’s white paper anniversary on October 31, marking 18 years since Satoshi Nakamoto introduced the cryptocurrency’s original design.

title: Hanwha secures $269 million U.S. Navy shipbuilding contract, eyes more orders
full_text:
Investing.com -- South Korea’s Hanwha Defense USA has secured a $269 million contract to build a medium landing ship for the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps, marking its first U.S. naval shipbuilding order since acquiring Philadelphia’s Philly Shipyard in 2024.
The agreement with U.S. maritime services company TOTE Services covers construction of one Medium Landing Ship (LSM), with options for three additional vessels.
The 2,687-ton, 100-meter ship is designed to support military operations in contested waters, including the Indo-Pacific region.
Construction at Hanwha Philly Shipyard is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027, with the program’s first vessel expected to be delivered in 2030.
Hanwha was selected through a competitive bidding process launched in July under TOTE Services’ vessel construction management program.
The company secured the contract based on competitive pricing and its acceptance of the program’s subcontract terms.
TOTE Services received a $2.2 billion contract earlier this year to oversee construction of up to eight vessels, supporting the Navy and Marine Corps’ planned 35-ship LSM fleet.
The program aims to expand U.S. naval shipbuilding capacity and accelerate deliveries through coordinated construction across multiple domestic shipyards.
Hanwha acquired Philly Shipyard in December 2024 and has since invested in workforce development and production technology to prepare the facility for military contracts.
The shipyard has previously delivered four National Security Multi-Mission Vessels under TOTE Services’ construction management model.
Hanwha Defense USA is also pursuing a controlling stake in the Philadelphia facility as part of its expansion into American defense manufacturing.
TOTE Services is continuing discussions with Bollinger Shipyards and Fincantieri Marinette Marine about their participation in the landing ship program.
The contract represents another step in Hanwha’s efforts to establish a stronger position in the U.S. defense shipbuilding market.

title: FBI links record $6.3 billion Binance crypto theft to North Korea
full_text:
Investing.com -- The FBI has accused North Korea of orchestrating the $6.3 billion cryptocurrency hack targeting Binance, identifying a state-linked hacking group responsible for previous major crypto thefts as the perpetrators.
The agency said Saturday that the North Korean hacking unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack, which ranks as the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
The FBI, working alongside the U.S. Secret Service and the Internal Revenue Service’s criminal investigation division, has been tracking movements of the stolen digital assets.
Investigators observed the hackers converting stolen cryptocurrencies primarily into Ethereum, with further laundering expected through decentralized finance platforms and instant cryptocurrency swap services.
The findings mark the first formal attribution of the Binance attack to North Korea following earlier speculation about the country’s involvement.
President Donald Trump said Friday that U.S. authorities were investigating whether North Korean hackers were behind the theft.
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, separately announced Saturday that it had covered approximately 90% of the $6.3 billion stolen in the attack.
The exchange expects to restore customer withdrawals by Sunday as it works to complete recovery efforts.
Binance reiterated that it would absorb the entire financial impact of the breach, promising that customers would not suffer losses from the incident.
The unprecedented theft has raised fresh concerns about security across the cryptocurrency industry as digital asset platforms seek broader institutional and retail adoption.
TraderTraitor has previously been linked to several high-profile cryptocurrency attacks, including the $1.5 billion theft from Bybit in 2025.
North Korean hackers have also been accused of carrying out a separate cryptocurrency theft worth approximately $620 million in 2022.
The FBI’s attribution comes amid renewed discussion of potential diplomatic engagement between Washington and Pyongyang.
Trump has recently suggested another meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could take place this year, although he later expressed uncertainty about whether either side was seeking talks.

title: What’s next for Euro bonds and the euro after Lagarde’s resignation?
full_text:
Investing.com -- European bond yields are expected to decline next year, and the euro could recover against the U.S. dollar, as ECB President Christine Lagarde’s early departure is unlikely to alter the central bank’s monetary policy outlook, according to UBS.
Lagarde announced her resignation effective February 7, 2027, hours before the European Central Bank held interest rates unchanged amid persistent inflation pressures and rising energy costs.
UBS expects a smooth leadership transition, arguing that inflation, wages, economic growth and financing conditions will remain the primary drivers of interest rates.
The ECB has raised rates twice this year, with inflation running at roughly double its 2% target.
Although policymakers have signaled further tightening may be necessary, UBS believes the central bank will wait for clearer evidence of persistent inflation before acting.
A December rate increase remains possible, particularly if higher energy prices trigger broader inflationary pressures.
Still, UBS expects Eurozone sovereign borrowing costs to decline into 2027, despite continued volatility in French government bonds.
France’s fiscal and political challenges could push sovereign spreads wider without credible budget consolidation.
UBS said the ECB could respond to disruptive market pressures through flexible reinvestment of maturing bonds, with its unused Transmission Protection Instrument providing another option.
The bank believes markets are pricing in excessive tightening, with expectations for another 75 basis points of ECB increases appearing difficult to justify.
It favors selectively extending duration in high-quality European bonds, particularly short- and medium-term maturities, including agency, covered and investment-grade corporate debt.
Longer maturities remain less attractive amid fiscal concerns and substantial bond issuance.
For currencies, UBS maintained its bullish euro outlook, forecasting EUR/USD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end.
The bank believes the euro’s recent decline has exceeded what underlying economic fundamentals would suggest.
Still, energy prices, monetary policy differences, sovereign spreads and geopolitical developments could keep currency markets volatile.
UBS also recommends progressively reducing excess U.S. dollar exposure where appropriate.

title: Saudi Arabia’s economy contracts 3.8% as war disrupts oil production
full_text:
Investing.com -- Saudi Arabia’s economy contracted for a second consecutive quarter as the war involving Iran and escalating conflict with Yemen’s Houthi rebels disrupted oil production and exports, threatening one of the kingdom’s weakest economic performances in years.
Gross domestic product declined 3.8% year over year in the third quarter, according to preliminary figures released Sunday by Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Statistics.
The contraction was smaller than the 4.7% decline recorded in the second quarter but marked the first consecutive quarterly declines since 2023.
Oil sector activity plunged 20.4%, improving from a 24.8% contraction in the previous quarter, as attacks on energy infrastructure continued to disrupt production and shipments.
Non-oil activity expanded 1.9%, highlighting the relative resilience of industries central to Saudi Arabia’s economic diversification strategy.
The figures reflect disruptions from the eight-month U.S.-Iran conflict, which has triggered attacks on Gulf energy facilities and restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Saudi Arabia has partially offset the disruption by redirecting crude shipments through a pipeline connecting its eastern oil fields to a Red Sea export terminal.
The third-quarter data also captures a temporary shutdown of that pipeline in September following attacks, but predates the subsequent recovery in Saudi crude exports to wartime highs.
The economic outlook has become more uncertain following an escalation in fighting between Saudi-led forces and the Iran-backed Houthis in October.
Houthi missile and drone attacks disrupted flights at Riyadh’s airport, forced changes to major investment events and interrupted activity in the capital’s financial district.
Although Brent crude has traded above $115 a barrel, concerns are increasingly shifting toward the impact of the conflict on non-oil businesses.
The International Monetary Fund said Saudi Arabia’s financial reserves and alternative oil-export infrastructure were helping cushion the economic damage, leaving the kingdom better positioned than several Gulf neighbors.
Saudi authorities previously projected a 3.6% economic contraction in 2026 and raised their expected budget deficit to 4.9% of GDP.

title: South Korea exports surge 93.7% in October, fastest growth since 1974
full_text:
Investing.com -- South Korea’s exports surged 93.7% in October from a year earlier, marking their strongest growth in more than five decades as booming semiconductor shipments and artificial intelligence demand powered overseas sales, government data showed Sunday.
Exports from Asia’s fourth-largest economy reached $115.28 billion, exceeding economists’ median forecast for a 93.2% increase.
The expansion accelerated from September’s 83.7% annual gain and represented the fastest export growth since January 1974, according to the trade ministry.
South Korea’s export performance is closely watched as an indicator of global trade conditions, particularly demand for electronics, semiconductors and other manufactured goods.
Semiconductor exports jumped 259.4% from a year earlier, supported by elevated chip prices and strong shipment volumes.
The trade ministry attributed the increase to sustained investment in computing infrastructure by major global technology companies competing for leadership in artificial intelligence.
Computer exports recorded an even sharper increase, soaring 496.6% as demand for servers supporting AI services continued to expand.
The figures highlight the growing contribution of AI-related technology spending to South Korea’s export performance, with semiconductor manufacturers benefiting from expanding data center investments.
The ministry also cited favorable calendar effects, as differences in the timing of the Chuseok holiday resulted in more working days during October than a year earlier.
That comparison helped amplify the annual growth rate, alongside strong underlying demand for technology products.
Imports also increased sharply, rising 36% year over year to $72.78 billion, compared with a 26% increase in September.
The import growth was the strongest since January 2022, reflecting a substantial acceleration in the value of goods entering the country.
South Korea recorded a trade surplus of $42.50 billion in October, down from the record $49.97 billion surplus registered in September.
The narrowing surplus came as import growth accelerated, although export revenues remained substantially higher than the country’s monthly import bill.

title: Who are the spillover winners from the AI export boom in Asia?
full_text:
Investing.com -- Taiwan is emerging as the biggest domestic beneficiary of Asia’s artificial intelligence export boom, followed by South Korea, as stronger technology demand boosts economic activity, government revenues and investment, according to Bank of America.
The bank said AI-related exports have become a major growth driver for Taiwan, South Korea and China, although the economic benefits are spreading unevenly across the three markets.
Year-to-date exports have increased 57% year over year in South Korea, 44% in Taiwan and 21% in China, according to BofA’s analysis.
Despite South Korea recording the strongest export growth, Taiwan is expected to experience the largest domestic spillover effects.
BofA attributed the differences to the relative size of each economy’s technology sector, production capacity constraints and broader economic conditions.
Taiwan’s substantial exposure to technology manufacturing means stronger external demand can translate into wider domestic economic gains.
South Korea also stands to benefit significantly, with the export expansion supporting domestic activity and government finances.
China is benefiting from stronger technology exports, but weaker domestic demand and economic headwinds are limiting the broader impact.
The differences are also shaping fiscal policy across the region.
BofA said rising exports have increased government tax revenues in all three economies, creating opportunities for additional public spending.
In Taiwan and South Korea, higher fiscal receipts are helping finance transfers and investment, providing another channel through which export growth supports domestic demand.
China has not experienced a comparable spending boost, partly reflecting financial constraints facing local governments.
The uneven economic effects are expected to produce different monetary policy responses.
In Taiwan and South Korea, stronger domestic demand and positive output gaps are adding to inflationary pressures, supporting the case for further interest rate increases.
China faces a different outlook, with softer domestic demand pointing toward additional monetary easing.
BofA’s assessment suggests Taiwan and South Korea are positioned to capture stronger economy-wide benefits from the AI boom, with China’s gains remaining more concentrated amid domestic challenges.

title: DeepSeek launches autonomous coding agent to challenge Anthropic’s Claude Code
full_text:
Investing.com -- Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek has introduced an open-source coding agent designed to operate more independently of human developers, intensifying competition with Anthropic’s Claude Code and other U.S. AI-powered programming tools.
The prototype, called Super-Agent, can monitor group conversations among software developers, identify coding problems and propose solutions without waiting for direct instructions, according to an announcement published Saturday by DeepSeek’s Harness team on WeChat.
Unlike conventional coding assistants that respond to individual prompts, the new system is designed to participate proactively in development workflows, reducing the need for constant human supervision.
DeepSeek said the agent’s objective is to minimize the attention required from users while maximizing the value delivered through automated assistance.
The company has made the prototype available as open-source software, allowing developers to examine its implementation and experiment with its capabilities.
The launch follows DeepSeek’s decision earlier this year to establish a dedicated Harness team focused on developing AI agents capable of competing with products from leading American AI laboratories.
In AI development, a harness refers to the software infrastructure surrounding a large language model that helps it coordinate tasks, interact with external tools, and execute more complex workflows.
Anthropic has used similar technology to develop Claude Code, which allows programmers to delegate coding assignments and other software development tasks to AI.
DeepSeek’s latest release reflects growing competition between Chinese and U.S. technology companies to develop increasingly capable and affordable AI systems.
The rivalry has expanded beyond conversational chatbots into autonomous agents designed to perform practical work for software engineers and business users.
DeepSeek is also strengthening its financial position as it prepares to compete with established AI developers.
The company raised approximately 100 billion yuan ($15 billion) in its latest funding round, one of China’s largest, ahead of a planned initial public offering.
The financing could support further investment in AI research and agent development as competition intensifies across the industry.

title: China’s Communist Party tightens oversight of officials
full_text:
BEIJING, Nov 1 (Reuters) - China’s ruling Communist Party has adopted measures aimed at tightening internal discipline, including stronger education about loyalty to the ruling party and closer oversight of officials, official Xinhua news agency reported on Sunday.
The decision calls for expanded study of party and national history, enhanced monitoring of cadres throughout their careers and stricter scrutiny of officials’ personal disclosures.
Authorities will verify cases in which family assets and spending appear to exceed normal income, while strengthening routine oversight of business activities involving senior officials’ spouses, children and children’s spouses, the report said.

title: Russian oil tankers deploy makeshift drone defenses amid Ukraine attacks - WSJ
full_text:
Investing.com -- Russian oil tankers are increasingly using protective nets, metal cages and rubber tires to defend against Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Moscow’s energy exports, The Wall Street Journal reported exclusively on Saturday.
At least 60 vessels equipped with makeshift anti-drone defenses have been documented passing through Istanbul’s Bosporus Strait since August, according to photographs reviewed by the newspaper.
The images, captured by maritime analyst Yoruk Isik, show tankers carrying protective structures around vulnerable areas, including engines, steering equipment, and bridge windows.
Nearly all the vessels identified are subject to U.S. or other Western sanctions for transporting Russian oil.
The defensive measures resemble equipment used on military vehicles and infrastructure in Ukraine, where drones have become a central weapon in the conflict.
Analysts said the nets and cages are intended to intercept incoming drones before they strike critical ship components.
Some vessels have also attached rubber tires along their sides to protect engines and rudders from attacks that could leave tankers disabled.
The modifications reflect growing concerns over Ukraine’s campaign against Russia’s shadow fleet, which transports oil outside conventional Western shipping and insurance arrangements.
Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, including refineries and oil tankers, seeking to reduce export revenues that help finance Moscow’s war effort.
The commander of Ukraine’s drone forces claimed in September that Ukrainian operations had disabled 300 Russian shadow-fleet vessels since July. That figure has not been independently verified.
Security analysts said the campaign could also place pressure on Russia’s financial system.
Many aging shadow-fleet tankers rely on insurance and financial backing from Russian state-supported banks, potentially exposing those institutions to losses from damaged vessels.
Ukraine escalated attacks on the fleet in 2025 as Washington pushed Kyiv and Moscow toward negotiations to end the war.
Russian oil shipments remain a major source of foreign currency for Moscow, making the tankers an economically significant target.

title: Macau gaming revenue falls 10% in October despite Golden Week visitor surge
full_text:
Investing.com -- Macau’s casino gaming revenue fell for a fifth consecutive month in October, as weaker spending by wealthy gamblers outweighed increased tourist arrivals during China’s Golden Week holiday.
Gross gaming revenue declined 10% from a year earlier to 21.68 billion patacas ($2.68 billion), according to figures released Sunday by Macau’s Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau.
The decline matched analysts’ median forecast and left gaming revenue approximately 18% below its pre-pandemic level in 2019.
October’s performance highlighted persistent weakness in Macau’s high-end gambling segment, which has struggled amid China’s economic slowdown and tighter scrutiny of wealthy residents’ overseas spending.
The downturn continued despite a strong recovery in tourist arrivals during the Golden Week holiday, traditionally one of the busiest periods for Macau’s casinos.
The gambling hub welcomed approximately 1.14 million visitors during the holiday, representing a 15.5% increase from the previous year.
Yet the additional visitors failed to generate a corresponding increase in gambling expenditure, according to analysts at Jefferies.
The figures suggest that stronger tourism demand has not been sufficient to offset reduced spending among higher-value casino customers.
Macau also recorded 3.2 million visitor arrivals in September, an increase of 16% year over year, indicating that tourism growth remained relatively resilient.
Complete visitor arrival figures for October are expected to be released later in November.
A cooling Chinese stock market has added to pressure on casino spending, reversing some of the wealth effects that supported gambling demand last year.
Macau’s gaming industry benefited from an artificial intelligence-driven equity market rally during the second half of 2025, which helped lift spending among affluent visitors.
That earlier recovery has also created tougher year-over-year comparisons for casino operators in 2026.
The prolonged slowdown affects major operators including Sands China, Galaxy Entertainment, Wynn Macau, MGM China and Melco International, which depend heavily on visitors from mainland China.
